description: The bar chart illustrates five distinct distribution patterns, comparing the relative values across different categories. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled as 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck,' in that order. The vertical axis represents the relative values, with a linear scale and no explicit label or units. Each category is represented by a group of three bars, colored in various shades of green, with the 'Increasing' distribution showing a steady rise in bar height from left to right, starting at a low value and ending at a high value. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of equal height across all three categories. The 'Decreasing' distribution exhibits a gradual decline in bar height, with the tallest bar on the left and the shortest on the right. The 'Spindle' distribution has the tallest bar in the center, with the outer bars being significantly shorter. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution displays the shortest bar at the center, with the outermost bars being taller. The bars within each category are not labeled or annotated, and there is no visible sorting or emphasis across the different distributions.

Each category is represented along the horizontal axis, with the vertical axis indicating the relative values of each distribution. The 'Increasing' distribution shows a steady rise in bar height from left to right, while the 'Decreasing' distribution exhibits a gradual decline in bar height. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of equal height across all categories. The 'Spindle' distribution has the tallest bars concentrated in the center, tapering off symmetrically toward the edges. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution displays the shortest bars at the center, with the outermost bars being approximately 50% taller than the central ones. Notably, the 'Spindle' distribution has the highest overall average bar height among all categories, exceeding the 'Increasing' distribution by roughly 20% on average.
